item.title: A First Closed-Form Robin Parameter for Optimized Schwarz Waveform Relaxation as a Function of Iteration Count, Overlap, and Time Window Length
item.description: arXiv:2611.05576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Schwarz waveform relaxation (SWR) is a parallel-in-time iterative method for the solution of evolution problems and belongs to the class of Parallel-in-Time algorithms that have received increasing attention over the past three decades. For parabolic problems, SWR converges linearly over long time intervals and exhibits superlinear convergence on short time intervals. Since the introduction of optimized variants (OSWR) nearly three decades ago, determining the optimized Robin parameter when OSWR is applied on bounded time windows has remained an open problem. We introduce here a new analytical approach that, for the first time, yields a closed-form expression for the optimal Robin parameter in the transmission conditions for the one-dimensional heat equation with two overlapping subdomains. The resulting formula explicitly characterizes the dependence of the optimal parameter on the iteration number, the overlap size, and the length of the time window. Beyond resolving this long-standing optimization problem, our analysis provides a framework that can be extended to more general settings, including higher-dimensional problems, multiple subdomains, and higher-order transmission conditions.
item.dc:creator: Alejandro Alfonso Rodriguez, Martin J. Gander, Felix Kwok

item.title: Comparative analysis of numerical methods for X-ray 3D reconstruction from sparse views
item.description: arXiv:2611.05645v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reconstruction of three-dimensional vascular structures from a limited number of X-ray projections is a severely underdetermined and ill-conditioned inverse problem. This work presents a unified matrix-free computational framework for evaluating iterative numerical methods for sparse-view cone-beam tomography. Forward and backprojection are implemented from ray-voxel intersection lengths computed with the Amanatides-Woo traversal algorithm, avoiding explicit construction of the large sparse system matrix. We systematically compare ART, SART, SIRT, gradient descent (GD), and Krylov subspace methods, including Conjugate Gradient, LSQR, and GMRES. The common matrix-free operators and geometry are used for all methods, allowing consistent comparisons under matched conditions. Particular emphasis is placed on gradient scaling using scalar step sizes, Jacobi preconditioning, and diagonal Hessian majorization, together with L1, Tikhonov, and total variation regularization. Numerical experiments use five three-dimensional coronary vessel models reconstructed from ten simulated X-ray projections under noise and scattering conditions, and are extended to real X-ray projections of a static thin-vessel phantom. Performance is evaluated in terms of convergence, computational cost, volumetric overlap, contrast-to-noise ratio, vessel diameter and centerline errors, and projection consistency at an unseen viewing angle. The results show that total-variation-regularized gradient descent with diagonal majorization provides the best overall reconstruction performance within the investigated computational budgets. By contrast, the tested Krylov implementations achieve limited geometric recovery despite higher computational cost. These findings emphasize the importance of appropriate gradient scaling and regularization for stable and computationally efficient sparse-view tomographic reconstruction.
item.dc:creator: Melitine N. Bardi, Konstantinos K. Delibasis

item.title: Discrete Poincar\'e and Bogovskii operators for higher order finite element de Rham complexes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present discrete Poincar\'e and Bogovskii operators for the common finite element discretizations of the de Rham complex of arbitrary polynomial order. We first discuss how such operators arise from a decomposition of the finite element spaces into a lowest order component and a remainder. This results in a fast algorithm for computing grad, curl, and div potentials. We then introduce a nonlocal Poincar\'e operator on contractible domains, which generalizes existing constructions based on cone operators to arbitrary order by integrating over cones against extended test forms. This requires developing commuting extension operators, which turn out to be related to rational forms. We also show how the nonlocal construction is modified to obtain a discrete Bogovskii operator preserving homogeneous boundary conditions. We further discuss how the ideas of the construction fit into the theory of finite element systems.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Guzm\'an, Pratyush Potu, K. Olav Tyssvang

item.title: Learning Coarse Spaces for Two-Grid Methods from Smoothed Errors with Applications to High-Contrast Porous Media Flow
item.description: arXiv:2611.05837v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Efficient two-grid solvers for high-contrast parametric elliptic problems require coarse spaces that capture error components poorly reduced by local smoothing. As these components vary with the problem parameters, repeatedly constructing parameter-adaptive coarse spaces can be computationally expensive. We propose a coarse-space learning method based on finite-step errors generated by additive Schwarz smoothing. For each training parameter, proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) of smoothed-error snapshots in the discrete energy inner product defines a reference coarse space. A continuous-coordinate neural generator is then trained using a basis-invariant, whitened subspace loss, enabling the prediction of parameter-adaptive coarse spaces on unseen grids. We establish discrete perturbation estimates relating coarse-space discrepancies to the associated nonsymmetric two-grid operators and derive conditional finite-step Krylov residual-polynomial bounds without assuming stationary energy contraction. Numerical experiments on high-contrast interface problems, moving-interface Darcy flow, and nonlinear Forchheimer flow demonstrate effective solver performance across varying parameters and grid resolutions. On the finest static test grid, with approximately 264 times as many degrees of freedom as the training grid, the learned spaces achieve FGMRES iteration counts close to those of parameter-specific POD references and comparable to GenEO spaces, while substantially reducing repeated coarse-space construction costs.
item.dc:creator: Chenglong Bao, Chen Cui, Ruohua Li

item.title: Dimensionally absolutely stable but non-diagonalizable $T$-meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.05923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct an infinite family of rectangular \(T\)-meshes whose conformality-vector-space dimension is constant over all structurally similar geometric realizations, although the meshes are not diagonalizable. For every integer \(d\ge 2\), the construction has \(2(d+2)\) \(\Tl\)-edges and intersection graph \(K_{d+2,d+2}\). Every \(\Tl\)-edge contains at least \(d+2\) vertices, so no edge is vanishable under the usual vertex-count criterion for bidegree \((d,d)\) and smoothness \((d-1,d-1)\). We prove that the conformality-vector space is one-dimensional throughout the structural similarity class. Its generator is the outer product of two vectors of barycentric interpolation weights, extended by four zero coordinates. Non-diagonalizability follows by examining the last edge in any proposed diagonalizing ordering. Thus, for the geometric structural similarity class specified here, diagonalizability is not a necessary condition for dimensional absolute stability.
item.dc:creator: Mao Shi

item.title: Magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields: a Fourier-finite difference approach
item.description: arXiv:2611.05950v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study magnetic Bloch eigenvalue problems for two-dimensional magnetic Schr\"odinger operators with nonuniform periodic magnetic fields and periodic scalar potentials, and develop a hybrid Fourier-finite difference discretization. A Landau-type gauge is constructed by solving a periodic Poisson equation. Under the integer magnetic flux condition, the magnetic Bloch boundary conditions are incorporated through shifts of Fourier-mode indices. The method combines link-variable-based covariant central differences in the $x$-direction with a Fourier pseudospectral discretization in the $y$-direction, yielding a Hermitian discrete Hamiltonian. The resulting eigenvalue problems are solved using a LOBPCG method. Under appropriate regularity assumptions, we establish a fully discrete consistency residual estimate of order $O(h_1^2+N_2^{-s})$. With suitable spectral separation and eigenspace dimension-preserving conditions, error estimates of the same order are derived for isolated eigenvalues and their associated eigenspaces. Numerical experiments show second-order convergence in the finite difference direction and rapid error reduction with increasing Fourier resolution, and illustrate band degeneracies and eigenstate distributions in nonuniform periodic magnetic fields.
item.dc:creator: Xueyang Li, Yuanwei Lai

item.title: Linear adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model
item.description: arXiv:2611.05977v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we propose a class of efficient, linear and decoupled adaptive variable time step schemes for the anisotropic phase field dendritic crystal growth model. The main difficulty is twofold: the gradient dependent anisotropic coefficient and the strongly nonlinear terms make unconditional energy stability difficult to achieve, and on nonuniform meshes the discrete energy dissipation law, which is straightforward to establish on uniform meshes, has to be reestablished under varying step sizes. To overcome these difficulties, two linear stabilizers and a time dependent auxiliary variable with relaxation are introduced and incorporated into a second-order generalized BDF-type operator, with the spatial derivatives discretized by the Fourier spectral method. The proposed schemes are energy stable for arbitrary positive adjacent step ratios, so that no restriction on the step ratio is imposed, and only two linear equations together with a few algebraic equations, which are solved independently in Fourier space, need to be solved at each time step. Moreover, the schemes are naturally compatible with energy based time adaptive strategies. The associated adaptive strategy reduces the number of time steps by $24.6\%$--$86.6\%$ in comparison with uniform time stepping, and numerical experiments on fourfold and sixfold dendritic growth in two dimensions and on three-dimensional growth confirm the accuracy, efficiency and stability of the proposed schemes.
item.dc:creator: Yayu Guo, Ziqi Ma

item.title: Geometric Multigrid Preconditioners for conforming Finite Element Methods on Arbitrarily Agglomerated Meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric multigrid methods for conforming finite element discretisations classically require a nested mesh hierarchy, forcing coarse meshes to be conforming, which is unsuitable for general domains. In order to eliminate this geometric constraint, we introduce and analyse a family of multilevel auxiliary space preconditioners. At the first level, a conforming Lagrangian discretisation on a fine simplicial mesh is preconditioned by a non-conforming polytopal discretisation posed on an arbitrarily agglomerated coarse mesh. At the subsequent levels, the coarse problem is solved by a geometric multigrid method for that polytopal discretisation on further agglomerated meshes, so that the whole hierarchy is generated from the fine mesh by agglomeration alone. We consider two polytopal discretisations, a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method and a hybrid high-order method. The prolongation operator at the first level is an element-wise interpolation onto the fine mesh followed by nodal averaging, preceded in the hybrid high-order case by a local potential reconstruction. For point-Jacobi and vertex-star patch additive Schwarz smoothers, we prove that the condition number of the preconditioned system is bounded by $O((H/h)^3)$, where $H/h$ is the coarsening ratio, and by $O((H/h)^2)$ for the DG variant with penalty proportional to $H/h$. Numerical experiments in two and three dimensions, on structured and unstructured meshes with agglomerates generated by automatic clustering algorithms, confirm the robustness of the preconditioners.
item.dc:creator: Santiago Badia, Jordi Manyer

item.title: Reconstruction and well-posedness of an inverse coefficient problem for a diffusion equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.
item.dc:creator: Siyu Cen, Bangti Jin, Yavar Kian, Zhi Zhou

item.title: Flux-Matched Poisson Iteration for Generated Jacobian Equations: Local Convergence and Spectral Galerkin Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.06153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a flux-matched Poisson iteration for solving generated Jacobian equations with second boundary conditions. In each step, it solves a fixed shifted Poisson problem with a Neumann-type boundary condition. Near a smooth regular solution with positive $C^{1,1}$ densities, we prove that the iteration has local geometric convergence in $C^{2,\alpha}$ on smooth connected Riemannian domains. The iteration is then discretized using a spectral Galerkin method, with local convergence proved for the Fourier-Jacobi scheme on spherical caps. Optical numerical experiments support these estimates and demonstrate useful imaging performance beyond the local convergence theory.
item.dc:creator: Haoxiang Zhang, Yixuan Zhang

item.title: Optimal Error Estimates With Polynomial Dependence on $\epsilon^{-1}$ for Mixed Finite Element Methods of the Cahn-Hilliard-Navier-Stokes System
item.description: arXiv:2611.06174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we analyze a first-order convex-splitting mixed finite element scheme for the Cahn--Hilliard--Navier--Stokes system, tracking explicitly how the error constants depend on the interface width $\epsilon$. Due to the strong nonlinear coupling inherent in the CHNS system and the singular dependence of the Cahn--Hilliard equation on $\epsilon$, conventional energy-based analyzes often lead to severe dependence of the error constants on $\epsilon^{-1}$, and may even result in exponential growth. Such dependence significantly limits the applicability of the resulting error estimates in the small-interfacial-thickness regime. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a robust parameter error analysis framework with respect to interfacial thickness $\epsilon$. In particular, by introducing $H^{-1}$ approximation properties for the Ritz projection and the Ritz and Stokes quasi-projection operators, together with spectral-type estimates for the discrete perturbed Cahn--Hilliard operator, we effectively control the singular terms arising from the interfacial thickness parameter in the error analysis. Compared with the classical results, which address only the Allen-Cahn or Cahn-Hilliard equation, we adopt a three-term discrete Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality analysis technique and achieve a substantial reduction in the degree of polynomial dependence for the coupled system. Numerical experiments are presented to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical results and to demonstrate the robustness of the method for different parameters of interfacial thickness.
item.dc:creator: Haijun Gao, Xi Li, Xiaoli Li

item.title: Optimal stability estimates and preasymptotic error analysis of the CIP-FEM for the Helmholtz equation with uniaxial perfectly matched layers
item.description: arXiv:2611.06288v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the uniaxial perfectly matched layer (UPML) problem for the Helmholtz equation in two and three dimensions and establish wavenumber-explicit stability estimates at high wavenumbers. For the full-space UPML problem, we prove the optimal stability estimate with the inf-sup constant satisfying $\mu_\infty\eqsim k^{-1}$ for sufficiently large $k$ if the absorption function $\sigma\in W^{1,\infty}$ is a piecewise-power function of order at least one for which $\|\sigma'\|_{L^\infty(\{t:0<\sigma(t)\leq\delta_*\})}\leq \varepsilon_*$, where $\varepsilon_*$ and $\delta_*$ depend only on the PML parameters. Using this stability estimate, we obtain the optimal inf-sup estimate $\mu_L\eqsim k^{-1}$ for the truncated UPML problem. These estimates further yield preasymptotic error estimates for a linear continuous interior penalty finite element method (CIP-FEM). Numerical simulations confirmed the theoretical predictions and demonstrated the effectiveness of CIP-FEM under high-wavenumber conditions.
item.dc:creator: Silin Wen, Yu Du

item.title: A weak Galerkin finite element method for the coupled Stokess-Biot problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.06335v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper,we consider a stable numerical method for the Stokes-Biot model. We adopt the standard formulation of the Stokes equations coupled with the mixed formulation of the Biot system involving the additional total pressure variable. We construct the semi-discrete scheme on polygonal meshes by employing weak Galerkin finite element methods for spatial discretization. It is convenient to incorporate the interface conditions into the semi-discrete scheme via the edge-based degrees of freedom. Furthermore, we give a fully discrete scheme based on the backward Euler method. We establish the well-posedness of these two schemes and provide a rigorous error analysis. Finally, we present some numerical examples to verify the convergence and stability of our algorithm under a wide range of some physical parameters.
item.dc:creator: Rui Li, Hui Peng, Xiuli Wang

item.title: A volume-conserving ALE continuous Galerkin method with residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann fluxes for nonlinear free-surface waves
item.description: arXiv:2611.06408v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an arbitrary Lagrangian--Eulerian continuous Galerkin finite element method for two-dimensional fully nonlinear free-surface potential flow. An isoparametric finite element method computes the interior potential on the current fluid domain, while a residual-based Dirichlet--Neumann flux drives the surface evolution. The residual-based flux satisfies a global discrete balance inherited from the interior variational formulation. When combined with compatible mesh motion, surface projection, and quadrature, this balance yields conservation of the discrete fluid volume at the semi-discrete level. An optional volume-conserving sixth-order surface dissipation controls high-frequency oscillations, and the surface equations are advanced with fourth-order Runge--Kutta integration, updating the mesh and interior solution at every stage. Numerical experiments confirm the expected spatial convergence for linear free-surface waves and demonstrate reduced mesh sensitivity for nonlinear waves over flat and curved bottoms. A rotating-wavemaker example further illustrates the treatment of moving solid boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Fan Wang, Yinhua Xia, Yan Xu

item.title: A Tensor-Network Chebyshev--Galerkin Method for Boundary-Value Problems in Computational Mechanics
item.description: arXiv:2611.06552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-inspired numerical methods for partial differential equations represent discretized fields and operators as quantics tensor trains (QTT), so that their cost depends on how compressible the problem is rather than on the number of unknowns. Global spectral formulations in this setting have so far relied on Fourier bases, restricted to periodic problems, or on collocation, which does not preserve the variational structure exploited by tensor-network solvers. We introduce a QTT Chebyshev--Galerkin method that assembles and solves global spectral systems directly in compressed form, without forming the underlying arrays. Starting from the weak formulation, the method handles coupled elliptic systems with variable coefficients, smoothly mapped geometries, and mixed Dirichlet--Robin boundary conditions, and yields symmetric positive-definite systems suited to variational tensor-network solvers. Parameters and random inputs enter as additional coordinates, so the same construction returns the solution over an entire parameter space in a single solve. In linear elasticity, the method retains spectral convergence and reaches errors below $10^{-8}$ on a three-dimensional benchmark, beyond those attained by QTT finite differences and Q2/Q4 FEniCSx finite elements over the tested range. A six-parameter cantilever design study covering $1.7\times10^{7}$ designs is solved in a single 92~s run, and a stochastic problem with ten random coordinates is represented with $2.4\times10^{6}$ times less memory than its full coefficient array.
item.dc:creator: Juan Jos\'e Rodr\'iguez-Aldavero, \'Angel de la Rosa Velasco, Juan Jos\'e Garc\'ia-Ripoll

item.title: Robust Multigrid on Adaptive Meshes for the Integral Fractional Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.06577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze a geometric multigrid method on locally refined mesh hierarchies for non-local variational problems, focusing on the integral fractional Laplacian. For newest-vertex-bisection-generated hierarchies, we prove uniform contraction of the multigrid iteration independently of the refinement level, the smallest local mesh size, and the polynomial degree in the finite element discretization. The proof is based on an abstract Hilbert-space framework, a strengthened Cauchy--Schwarz estimate obtained from a near-/far-field decomposition of the non-local bilinear form, and a multilevel stable decomposition independent of the discretization parameters. Numerical experiments underline the theoretical findings.
item.dc:creator: Markus Faustmann, Paula Hilbert, Ani Mira\c{c}i, Dirk Praetorius

item.title: Sobolev--Poincar\'e inequalities for piecewise $W^{2,p}$ functions over general polytopic meshes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish Sobolev--Poincar\'e inequalities for piecewise $W^{2,p}$ functions in two and three dimensions over families of general polytopic (including shape-regular simplicial and Cartesian) meshes, allowing for degenerate facets. The proposed inequalities feature control by either the broken Hessian or, more naturally for general fourth-order problems, the broken Laplacian. Important tools in their derivation are a Helmholtz decomposition in Banach--Sobolev spaces and Sobolev--Poincar\'e inequalities for piecewise $W^{1,p}$ functions; we avoid the use of any inverse inequality. We provide estimates with fairly general Lebesgue exponents. Applications to the stability analysis of nonconforming discretizations for second- and fourth-order, linear and nonlinear problems are exhibited.
item.dc:creator: Michele Botti, Lorenzo Mascotto

item.title: To lift or not to lift: Operator inference for nonlinear PDEs with boundary control
item.description: arXiv:2611.06665v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Operator inference (OpInf) provides a nonintrusive framework for learning projection-based reduced-order models directly from data, but its standard formulations do not explicitly account for the fact that boundary actuation changes the admissible solution space of a PDE. This paper develops and evaluates a boundary-consistent, lifting-based OpInf formulation for nonlinear PDEs with time-varying inhomogeneous boundary conditions. The proposed approach decomposes the state into a known lifting component that satisfies the prescribed boundary conditions and a homogeneous component represented in a POD basis. Substituting this decomposition into the governing dynamics reveals a boundary-consistent reduced model structure in which the learned dynamics includes bilinear state-input and quadratic input-input interactions for quadratically nonlinear PDEs. The resulting operators are inferred from data, preserving the nonintrusive character of OpInf while guaranteeing boundary condition satisfaction by construction. Numerical experiments on boundary-actuated heat, Burgers, and lid-driven cavity problems show that the lifted formulation improves boundary compliance and can enhance prediction accuracy, solver stability, and computational efficiency, although these gains vary across problems and reduced model dimensions. Overall, this study establishes lifting as a principled extension of OpInf for boundary-actuated PDEs, clarifies when and how this formulation improves performance, and indicates that standard OpInf can remain an effective alternative in certain regimes.
item.dc:creator: Zhuoyuan Wang, Yorie Nakahira, Wael H. Ali, Saviz Mowlavi

item.title: Improving the performance of regularized Stokeslet simulations using Rosenbrock time integration methods
item.description: arXiv:2611.05428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The method of regularized Stokeslets (MRS) is widely used to model fluid-structure interactions of microscopic bodies in viscous environments. Specifically, MRS computes the fluid velocity generated by regularized forces distributed on an immersed body, which in turn defines a system of ordinary differential equations with which to evolve the body so that the no-slip condition is enforced. To accurately model material properties such as elasticity and bending rigidity, the resulting ODE system is often stiff and, therefore, computationally expensive to solve with explicit time-integration methods. Here we demonstrate the potential of linearly implicit Rosenbrock (ROS) time integration methods to greatly reduce the computational time required to solve such ODE systems. We focus on the classic model problem of the swimming of a flexible filament driven by preferred curvature forcing. Our findings indicate that, compared to previous MRS simulations, the increased stability of ROS methods allows for speed-ups between twenty and two thousand times over explicit Runge-Kutta (ERK) methods. Moreover, we present approximate scaling laws for this speedup as a function of the key model parameters (bending rigidity and slenderness) at the root of numerical stiffness. Lastly, beyond the basic ROS approach, we discuss several additional strategies that further improve performance.
item.dc:creator: Moslem Uddin, Lisa J. Fauci, Ricardo Cortez, Tommaso Buvoli

item.title: Largest-Angle Bisection and Statistical Regularization of Triangle Shapes
item.description: arXiv:2611.06492v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Largest-angle bisection (LAB) repeatedly divides a triangle by bisecting its largest angle. Although this procedure is known to preserve nondegenerate triangle shapes, less is known about the distribution of shapes across the resulting refinement tree. We show that its long-term behavior is governed by a distinction between pure and mixed branches. A branch that eventually selects only one of the two children may approach an exceptional family of shapes. By contrast, every branch that changes children infinitely often converges in shape to a right-isosceles triangle. This follows from a projective Lyapunov function that is non-increasing at every refinement and decreases strictly whenever the selected child changes. Consequently, a random branch converges to the right-isosceles shape with probability one, and the proportion of triangles near that shape tends to one across complete refinement levels. Largest-angle bisection therefore produces statistical regularization even though exceptional branches remain present.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\^ome Michaud

item.title: On Spectral Clustering in Algebraic Multigrid Methods
item.description: arXiv:2511.12298v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a new direct multilevel method for solving general nonsingular complex square linear systems admitting a suitable block partition, using a regular smoother and an arbitrary but equal number of pre- and post-smoothings. Through careful analysis of the error propagation operator, we cluster the spectrum of this operator. This allows us to write a direct K-cycle version of the method.
item.dc:creator: Jose Pablo Lucero Lorca, Conor McCoid, Michal Outrata

item.title: A semi-generating function approach to the stability of implicit-explicit multistep methods for nonlinear parabolic equations
item.description: arXiv:2605.05619v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rigorous stability analysis of high-order implicit-explicit linear multistep (IELM) methods for nonlinear parabolic equations by using discrete energy arguments is a long standing open issue due to their non-A-stability property. A novel semi-generating function approach combined with a global discrete energy analysis is suggested for the stability and convergence of general IELM methods in solving nonlinear parabolic equations. Inspired from the Grenander-Szeg\H{o} theorem for Toeplitz matrices, the semi-generating function approach is used to handle the three groups of discrete coefficients via three complex polynomials on the unit circle. A unified theoretical framework is then presented to establish the unconditional stability of IELM methods if the minimum eigenvalue of composite convolution kernels for the implicit part is properly large and the spectral norm bound of composite convolution kernels for the explicit part is properly small. An indicator, called implicit-explicit controllability intensity, is then introduced to evaluate the degree of controllability of the implicit part over the explicit part. Some of the existing IELM methods, up to fifth-order time accuracy, are revisited and compared by computing the associated implicit-explicit controllability intensities such that one can choose an IELM method or proper parameter to maintain the unconditional stability for a specific nonlinear parabolic model. We also propose a new parameterized class of IELM methods, up to the ninth-order time accuracy, which satisfy the a priori settings of our theory and have a large value of the implicit-explicit controllability intensity by choosing a proper parameter so that they would be well suited for a wide class of nonlinear parabolic problems.
item.dc:creator: Hong-lin Liao, Chaoyu Quan, Tao Tang, Tao Zhou

item.title: Element-wise Convergence Behavior of Subspace Iteration
item.description: arXiv:2609.21540v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies the element-wise convergence behavior of subspace iteration. All results are established for both \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R}\) and \(\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{C}\). For a diagonal matrix \(\Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n)\) with \(|\lambda_1|>\cdots>|\lambda_n|>0\), we analyze the modulus of each entry of the iterative matrix sequence generated by subspace iteration, both without and with the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure. Under mild assumptions on the initial matrix \(X\in\mathbb{F}^{n\times m}\), we first derive exact asymptotic expressions for \(|Q_k(i,j)|\) in the subspace iteration without the Rayleigh--Ritz procedure: entries with \(i\neq j\) decay as \(|\lambda_{\max\{i,j\}}/\lambda_{\min\{i,j\}}|^k\), and the deviation of \(|Q_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \(\max\{|\lambda_j/\lambda_{j-1}|,|\lambda_{j+1}/\lambda_j|\}^{2k}\), with explicit coefficients determined by the LU factorization of \(X\). Similar conclusions could also be established for upper triangular matrices. For the Rayleigh--Ritz variant, we obtain element-wise asymptotic formulas for the normalized Ritz vectors \(Z_k\). Specifically, for \(|Z_k(i,j)|\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\geq m+1\) decay as \(|\lambda_i/\lambda_j|^k\), off-diagonal entries with \(i\leq m\) decay as \(|\lambda_{m+1}^2/(\lambda_i\lambda_j)|^k\), and the deviation of \(|Z_k(j,j)|\) from \(1\) decays as \(|\lambda_{m+1}/\lambda_j|^{2k}\). These results give an element-wise description of the convergence behavior of subspace iteration. After an orthogonal or unitary change of basis, the results could be further generalized.
item.dc:creator: Mingyang Zhao

item.title: Deep-Learning Solvers and Surrogates for Infinity and p-Laplace Problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.30809v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the use of neural network solvers for infinity and $p$-Laplace problems, which are fundamental in nonlinear analysis and have practical applications. Our approach employs Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) to address computational challenges associated with large $p$ values, ranging from $2$ to $1000$, on various 2D and 3D domains. Our method offers advantages over traditional physics-based solvers, especially in three dimensions where mesh-based solvers become very costly for these problems. We also establish conditional convergence results for PINN approximations of both problems and a universal approximation result for DeepONet on the parametric $p$-Poisson problem. We demonstrate the effectiveness of these neural network solvers through numerical experiments and compare their performance with conventional methods.
item.dc:creator: Tak Shing Au Yeung, Ka Chun Cheung, Hannah Potgieter, Steven J. Ruuth, Simon See

item.title: Stochastic Gradient Leimkuhler-Matthews Integrator with Second Order Discretization Error
item.description: arXiv:2610.24781v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) has a discretization error of first order in the step size $h$, even with the full gradient. We study the stochastic gradient Leimkuhler--Matthews (SGLM) integrator, which has the same cost as SGLD, one stochastic gradient per step, and reuses each Gaussian vector in consecutive steps. With the full gradient, SGLM is the Leimkuhler--Matthews (LM) integrator, whose discretization error for the invariant distribution is of second order. For a potential strongly convex outside a ball, we prove the bound $\mathcal O(\frac{1}{Nh} + \Sigma^2 h^2 + h^4)$ on the mean square error (MSE) of time averages of SGLM over $N$ steps, where $\Sigma$ bounds the variance of the gradient noise. The proof uses a modified class that absorbs the non-Markovian part of SGLM. The discretization error enters this bound as $h^4$ and the MSE bound of SGLD as $h^2$, while a larger batch reduces only the term $\Sigma^2 h^2$ in both bounds. In Bayesian logistic regression on MNIST, SGLM has a smaller estimated MSE than SGLD. The coefficient of $h$ in the numerical bias of SGLM is given explicitly by the covariance of the gradient noise and the continuous Poisson equation. The coefficient for SGLD contains in addition the Hessian of the potential, which comes from the discretization error. Through Riesz representors, the coefficients of the numerical bias determine the coefficients of the Wasserstein-1 errors of SGLM and SGLD.
item.dc:creator: Xuda Ye, Yuliang Wang, Guang Lin, Cindy Xiangrui Kong

item.title: First- and second-order constrained optimisation for inverse homogenisation of unidirectionally varying microstructure
item.description: arXiv:2611.03372v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is concerned with inverse homogenisation problems that aim to identify microstructure features of a body from macroscopic measurements. The unknown microstructure is assumed to vary macroscopically in one spatial direction and affects the effective tensor in an elliptic partial differential equation that governs the behaviour of the body on the macroscale. We establish the well-posedness of the PDE-constrained minimisation problems that model the task of identifying the microstructure, derive first-order necessary optimality conditions, and prove the convergence of a gradient-projection algorithm for the studied problem class in an infinite-dimensional setting. We moreover demonstrate that recently obtained results on generalised differentiability properties of solution maps of bilateral obstacle problems make it possible to set up and analyse a novel semismooth Newton method in the considered situation. The functional analytic setting that we use for our investigation is chosen such that it covers various elliptic PDEs simultaneously (classical second-order equations, bi-Laplace problems, linear elasticity, etc.) and explicitly exploits the problem structure to obtain global convergence guarantees for the studied solution algorithms in terms of the Lipschitz constants of the involved operators. Our analysis is accompanied by numerical experiments which show that the new semismooth Newton approach requires far less expensive projection evaluations than the gradient-descent method and, thus, offers a significant speedup.
item.dc:creator: Constantin Christof, Malte A. Peter, Michael Ulbrich

item.title: Model-Adaptive Simulation of Hierarchical Shallow Water Moment Equations in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2510.25351v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Shallow free surface flows are often characterized by both subdomains that require high modeling complexity and subdomains that can be sufficiently accurately modeled with low modeling complexity. Moreover, these subdomains may change in time as the water flows through the domain. This motivates the need for space and time adaptivity in the simulation of shallow free surface flows. In this paper, we develop the first adaptive simulations using the recently developed Shallow Water Moment Equations, which are an extension of the standard Shallow Water Equations that allow for vertically changing velocity profiles by including additional variables and equations. The model-specific modeling complexity of a shallow water moment model is determined by its order. The higher the order of the model, the more variables and equations are included in the model. Shallow water moment models are ideally suited for adaptivity because they are hierarchical such that low-order models and high-order models share the same structure. To enable adaptive simulations, we propose two approaches for the coupling of the varying-order shallow water moment equations at their boundary interfaces. The first approach dynamically updates padded state variables but cannot be written in conservative form, while the second approach uses fixed padded state variable values of zero and reduces to conservative form for conservative moment equations. The switching procedure between high-order models and low-order models is based on a new set of model error estimators, originating from a decomposition of the high-order models. Numerical results of a dam break and of the collision of a dam-break wave with a smooth wave for different friction parameter values yield accurate results, while achieving speedups up to 40 percent compared to a non-adaptive model with fixed modeling complexity.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Verbiest, R., Koellermeier, J. Model-Adaptive Simulation of Hierarchical Shallow Water Moment Equations in One Dimension, Comput. Math. Appl., 221, 135-158, 2026
item.dc:creator: Rik Verbiest, Julian Koellermeier

item.title: Efficient Receding Horizon Control for Stabilizing 2D Navier--Stokes Flows with Finitely Many Localized Actuators and POD Acceleration
item.description: arXiv:2604.15846v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper develops and analyzes a computationally efficient receding horizon control (RHC) strategy for steering two-dimensional Navier--Stokes flows to prescribed reference trajectories. The control is represented by a finite linear combination of localized actuators supported within a prescribed control subdomain. At the continuous PDE level, we establish local exponential stabilization in the $L^2$-norm and suboptimality of the actuator-based RHC scheme for weak solutions. Direct implementation requires the repeated solution of high-dimensional finite-horizon optimal control problems. To reduce this computational cost, we combine RHC with model order reduction based on proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). A common POD space constructed from state snapshots reduces the state and adjoint equations and accelerates the online optimization, while the resulting controls are applied to the full-order discretized dynamics. Numerical experiments for two flow configurations of increasing complexity examine the influence of actuator layouts, prediction horizons, viscosity, and POD dimension. The numerical results demonstrate substantial reductions in computational cost while maintaining closed-loop stabilization in the tested configurations.
item.dc:creator: Behzad Azmi, Stefan Frei, Felix Sauer

item.title: Medial Axis Aware Learning of Signed Distance Functions
item.description: arXiv:2604.16512v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We propose a novel variational method to compute a highly accurate global signed distance function (SDF) to a given point cloud. To this end, the jump set of the gradient of the SDF, which coincides with the medial axis of the surface, is explicitly taken into account through a higher-order variational formulation that enforces linear growth along the gradient direction away from this discontinuity set. The eikonal equation and the zero-level set of the SDF are enforced as constraints. To make this variational problem computationally tractable, a phase field approximation of Ambrosio-Tortorelli type is employed. The associated phase field function implicitly describes the medial axis. The method is implemented for surfaces represented by unoriented point clouds using neural network approximations of both the SDF and the phase field. Experiments demonstrate the method's accuracy both in the near field and globally. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons with other approaches show the advantages of the proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Weidemaier, Christoph Norden-Smoch, Martin Rumpf

item.title: Theoretical guarantees for stochastic gradient sampling methods via Gaussian convolution inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2604.24632v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive first-order (in the stepsize) bounds on the bias in Wasserstein distances of the invariant measure of stochastic gradient kinetic Langevin dynamics with minimal assumptions on the stochastic gradient noise. These bounds sharpen existing non-asymptotic guarantees for stochastic-gradient MCMC methods and provide a quantitative resolution of a previously open problem on invariant measure accuracy. The main technical ingredients are new Gaussian convolution inequalities controlling the Wasserstein-$p$ distance between a Gaussian convolved with a mean-zero perturbation and the Gaussian itself. We anticipate that these inequalities will be of independent interest beyond the present application. To complement the theory, we illustrate the benefits of stochastic gradient sampling methods on a one-dimensional model, a Bayesian logistic regression example and a Bayesian random-effect model including comparison with pseudo-marginal MCMC methods.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Paulin, Peter A. Whalley

item.title: Quantum estimates for classical polynomial optimization
item.description: arXiv:2607.25445v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The problem of finding lower and upper bounds on multivariate homogeneous polynomials is both difficult and important given its applications to questions ranging from dynamical stability in complex potential landscapes to data analysis. From the standpoint of tensor eigenvalue theory, the question is equivalent to finding the smallest and the largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor corresponding to the given polynomial. Standard approaches outlined in the literature amount to running nonlinear iterations in search for the optimal rays along which the growth of the polynomial is fastest or slowest. Unlike the case of matrices (or their corresponding multivariate quadratic forms) convergence of such algorithms for higher-rank tensors is capricious due to the complex topography of polynomial objective functions. In this essay, a very different strategy, inspired by quantum-mechanical variational methods, is introduced for finding bounds on polynomials. The original polynomial is replaced by an operator acting in a suitably chosen (large) space of states, such that in an appropriate "classical" limit this operator approaches the original polynomial expression made of commutative variables. As a result, approximating the smallest and largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor, and thus finding bounds on polynomials, amounts to diagonalizing the resulting quantum operator, represented as a large matrix, and then inspecting the smallest and largest eigenvalues of this matrix. This approach is then successfully applied to standard test examples from tensor eigenvalue literature and other problems of interest in mathematical physics including Strichartz-type inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Evnin

item.title: On solid angles and simplex shape measures
item.description: arXiv:2610.05883v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The minimum solid angle of a simplex is shown to be a shape measure in any dimension. While this has been known in dimensions two and three, the higher-dimensional generalization is new. We prove inequalities between the minimum solid angle of a non-degenerate simplex and its fullness. Up to dimension-dependent constants, the fullness is bounded from above by the minimum solid angle, and it is bounded from below by the square of the minimum solid angle. The exponents are optimal for three and higher dimensions. This work therefore generalizes the minimum angle condition. We also review several simplex shape measures and their relationships.
item.dc:creator: Martin W. Licht
